summary.text: At \(n=8=2^3\), one has \(\Omega(8)=3\), which is odd and at least \(3\), but Möbius inversion gives \(a(8)=8!\,(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\). Thus the asserted condition does not imply negativity.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n\frac1j
\]
be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. The sequence is characterized by
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}\frac{a(k)}{k!}=H_n
\qquad(n\ge 1).
\]
Put \(b(k)=a(k)/k!\). Then the defining identity says
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}b(k)=H_n.
\]
By Möbius inversion,
\[
b(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
where \(\mu\) is the ordinary Möbius function. Consequently,
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, this is the standard divisor-sum inversion: the Möbius function is the inverse, under Dirichlet convolution, of the constant function \(1\), so applying it to the relation \(H_n=\sum_{d\mid n}b(d)\) gives the displayed expression for \(b(n)\).

We disprove the conjecture by taking
\[
n=8.
\]
This is a positive integer, and its prime factorization is
\[
8=2^3.
\]
Therefore the total number of prime factors counted with multiplicity is
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
In particular, \(\Omega(8)\) is odd and is at least \(3\). Thus the right-hand side of the conjectured equivalence is true at \(n=8\).

It remains to determine the sign of \(a(8)\). The positive divisors of \(8\) are
\[
1,2,4,8.
\]
Formula (1) therefore becomes
\[
\begin{aligned}
a(8)
&=8!\bigl(\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
The Möbius values in this expression are
\[
\mu(8)=0,\qquad \mu(4)=0,\qquad \mu(2)=-1,\qquad \mu(1)=1.
\]
The first two values are zero because both \(8\) and \(4\) are divisible by the square \(2^2\). The value at the prime \(2\) is \(-1\), and by definition \(\mu(1)=1\). Hence all terms except those involving \(H_4\) and \(H_8\) vanish, and
\[
a(8)=8!\,(H_8-H_4). \tag{2}
\]

The required harmonic numbers are
\[
H_4=1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac14=\frac{25}{12}
\]
and
\[
H_8=1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac14+\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18
=\frac{761}{280}.
\]
For example, with common denominator \(840\), the numerator of \(H_8\) is
\[
840+420+280+210+168+140+120+105=2283,
\]
so \(H_8=2283/840=761/280\). Likewise, \(H_4=25/12=1750/840\). Therefore
\[
H_8-H_4
=\frac{2283-1750}{840}
=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
Since \(8!=40320\), equation (2) gives
\[
a(8)=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}
=48\cdot533
=25584.
\]
Thus
\[
a(8)=25584>0,
\]
so the assertion \(a(8)<0\) is false.

At \(n=8\), therefore, the condition “\(\Omega(n)\) is odd and at least \(3\)” is true, because \(\Omega(8)=3\), whereas the condition \(a(n)<0\) is false, because \(a(8)=25584\). The two conditions are not equivalent for all positive integers. Hence the conjecture is false.
